record.original_question: Does there exist any query-memory tradeoff (T,M) for convex Lipschitz optimization with limited memory that lies polynomially inside the currently unknown region between the two known extremes, namely the gradient-descent regime with memory on the order of d log(LB/epsilon) bits and query complexity on the order of 1/epsilon^2, and the center-of-mass regime with query complexity on the order of d log(1/epsilon) and memory on the order of d^2 log^2(LB/epsilon)? Or is every tradeoff in that intermediate square impossible?

evidence.quote: We do not know whether any trade-offs inside the "?" square are possible or not.
Question 4 ($100 or Michelin Bib Gourmand Meal) Resolve the possibility or impossibility of some trade-off (T, M) polynomially inside the unknown square in Figure 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of minimizing a convex 1-Lipschitz function f: B → ℝ on the unit ball B ⊂ ℝ^d (with respect to the Euclidean norm), to additive accuracy ε, using a first-order oracle that on query x ∈ B returns the pair (f(x), g) with g a subgradient of f at x. An algorithm is permitted T such oracle queries and may retain at most M bits of internal state between queries; it must output a point x̂ ∈ B with f(x̂) − inf_{x ∈ B} f(x) ≤ ε with high probability over its internal randomness.

Two known regimes for (T, M) are:
(i) Gradient descent, achieving T = O(1/ε²) queries with M = O(d · log(LB/ε)) bits of memory (where L = 1 is the Lipschitz constant and B = 1 is the radius of the domain, kept symbolic to indicate scaling).
(ii) Center-of-mass / cutting-plane methods, achieving T = O(d · log(1/ε)) queries with M = O(d² · log²(LB/ε)) bits of memory.

Question: Does there exist any algorithm whose query-memory pair (T, M) lies polynomially strictly between these two extremes — that is, with T = poly(d, 1/ε) strictly larger (in the relevant scaling) than O(d log(1/ε)) and strictly smaller than O(1/ε²), and M correspondingly strictly between O(d log(LB/ε)) and O(d² log²(LB/ε)) — or, conversely, is every such intermediate tradeoff ruled out by an unconditional lower bound?
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Marsden, Sharan, Sidford and Valiant (2022) showed any first-order algorithm needs either Ω(d^{2-δ}) memory or Ω(d^{1+δ/6-o(1)}) queries for quasi-polynomially small ε, ruling out part of the unknown region. Blanchard, Zhang and Jegelka (2023) gave memory-constrained cutting-plane algorithms achieving O(d²/p · log(1/ε)) bits with O((Cd/p · log(1/ε))^p) queries, providing nontrivial intermediate tradeoffs. Subsequent work (Blanchard et al., 2023) established quadratic memory is necessary for optimal query complexity, showing center-of-mass is Pareto-optimal in that regime. The full tradeoff curve across the entire intermediate square is not yet completely characterized.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Convex Optimization Requires Superlinear Memory
status_evidence.snippet: Any randomized first-order algorithm minimizing a d-dimensional 1-Lipschitz convex function must use Ω(d^{2-δ}) memory or Ω(d^{1+δ/6-o(1)}) queries.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes lower bounds inside the previously unknown region, ruling out certain intermediate tradeoffs.

status_evidence.title: Memory-Constrained Algorithms for Convex Optimization via Recursive Cutting-Planes
status_evidence.snippet: Memory-constrained cutting-plane algorithms use O(d²/p ln(1/ε)) bits of memory and O((C d/p ln(1/ε))^p) oracle calls.
status_evidence.claim: Provides nontrivial intermediate query/memory tradeoffs, partially answering the open question affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Memory Is Necessary for Optimal Query Complexity in Convex Optimization: Center of Mass Is Pareto Optimal
status_evidence.snippet: Quadratic memory is required to achieve optimal query complexity; center-of-mass is Pareto optimal.
status_evidence.claim: Shows the center-of-mass regime cannot be improved without sacrificing memory.

status_evidence.title: Memory-Query Tradeoffs for Randomized Convex Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes memory-query tradeoffs for randomized convex optimization.
status_evidence.claim: Further refines the tradeoff in the intermediate region.
